.gitignore
version 4

`typescript-eslint@8.70.0` declara peerDependency `typescript: ">=4.8.4 <6.1.0"`, pero en `package.json` se permite `typescript: ^6.0.3` (lo que habilita `6.1.x` en adelante). Eso puede romper la instalación o generar warnings cuando se actualicen dependencias.

Los scripts `lint`/`lint:fix` usan `eslint .` sin `--ext`, lo que hace que ESLint (v10) no incluya archivos TypeScript (`.ts/.mts/.cts`) al recorrer directorios; esto contradice el objetivo de “soporte completo para TypeScript”.

Al incorporar `eslint@10.9.1`, el árbol de dependencias exige Node `^20.19.0 || ^22.13.0 || >=24`; sin un campo `engines` en `package.json`, es fácil que alguien intente instalar con una versión menor y falle el `npm install`/`npm ci` por incompatibilidad de engines.
Aprovechando que este proyecto arranca de cero, coloquemos nombres de variables y funciones en ingles.

comments.body: In this project section, the external links use target="_blank" without rel="noopener noreferrer". Please add the rel attribute to both links to mitigate reverse-tabnabbing.
This link uses target="_blank" without rel="noopener noreferrer". Add rel to mitigate reverse-tabnabbing for external links.
This link uses target="_blank" without rel="noopener noreferrer". Add rel to mitigate reverse-tabnabbing for external links.
This link uses target="_blank" without rel="noopener noreferrer". Add rel to mitigate reverse-tabnabbing for external links.
bcryptjs is a password hashing library, not encryption. Describing it as “encryption” is technically inaccurate; consider rewording to refer to password hashing (and keep JWT as token-based auth).
Links opened with target="_blank" should include rel="noopener noreferrer" to prevent reverse-tabnabbing and avoid leaking window.opener. Please add the rel attribute to these external links.
These GitHub links use target="_blank" without rel="noopener noreferrer". Add the rel attribute to mitigate reverse-tabnabbing (window.opener) when navigating to external pages.
This link uses target="_blank" without rel="noopener noreferrer". Please add rel to avoid reverse-tabnabbing and ensure window.opener is not exposed to the destination page.

The visual separators ("|") are included as literal text nodes in spans, so screen readers will announce them. Consider making separators presentational (e.g., aria-hidden="true" on the separator spans) or applying separators via CSS to improve accessibility.
Links opened with target="_blank" should also include rel="noopener noreferrer" to prevent reverse-tabnabbing and to avoid leaking window.opener to the external site.

The live demo link uses plain HTTP. Since this is a public CV/README and Vercel supports TLS, switch the demo URL to HTTPS to avoid mixed-content warnings and to prevent users from being sent over an unencrypted connection.

English wording is ungrammatical: "Designed to enterprise security and privacy standards". Consider rephrasing to something like "Designed to meet enterprise security and privacy standards" for clarity and professionalism.

Unused import TableHeaderCell.

The icon rendering logic is incorrect. The expression `currentContext.primary.icon || ImportedIcons[currentContext.primary.icon?.name]` will always evaluate to `currentContext.primary.icon` because it's already a reference to the icon component (e.g., ImportedIcons.PeopleIcon). The fallback using `ImportedIcons[currentContext.primary.icon?.name]` will never execute. Since `currentContext.primary.icon` is already the correct component reference, this should simply be `React.createElement(currentContext.primary.icon, { size: 24 })`.

The icon rendering logic is incorrect. The expression `sec.icon || ImportedIcons[sec.icon?.name]` will always evaluate to `sec.icon` because it's already a reference to the icon component. The fallback using `ImportedIcons[sec.icon?.name]` will never execute. Since `sec.icon` is already the correct component reference, this should simply be `React.createElement(sec.icon, { size: 14 })`.
Unused import OfficeRibbonWithTitle.
Unused import TableHeaderCell.
Unused import OfficeRibbonWithTitle.

OfficeRibbon should not be exported from the atoms index file because it doesn't exist in the atoms directory. OfficeRibbon has been moved to the organisms directory. This export will cause an error. The correct export should be from the organisms index file instead.

The SVG path for ShieldIcon appears to be corrupted or truncated. There's a malformed section in the path data (`.72.04 1.41.1.1.94.78 1.04 1.2.38 1.34-.32.03-.1.08-.2.13-.3z`) that contains incomplete coordinate values and appears to be missing proper path commands. This should be reviewed against the original Bootstrap Icons implementation to ensure the icon renders correctly.

The inline IIFE for rendering icons is unnecessarily complex and reduces code readability. Since the icon property already contains the component reference, a simpler approach would be to directly use React.createElement or JSX syntax. Consider refactoring to: `React.createElement(currentContext.primary.icon, { size: 24 })` or creating a separate helper function to render icons.

The organisms index file is missing exports for OfficeTable and VaccinationDetails components, which are imported in several view files (VaccinationList.jsx, StaffList.jsx, GuardianList.jsx, MeetingMinutesList.jsx, DocumentReviewList.jsx, AttendanceList.jsx, ActivityList.jsx, ClassroomList.jsx). This will cause runtime errors when these views try to use these components.

The icon rendering logic is incorrect. The expression `action.icon || ImportedIcons[action.icon?.name]` will always evaluate to `action.icon` because it's already a reference to the icon component. The fallback using `ImportedIcons[action.icon?.name]` will never execute. Since `action.icon` is already the correct component reference, this should simply be `React.createElement(action.icon, { size: 14 })`.

The SVG paths for PeopleFillIcon appear to be incomplete. The second path element has coordinate values starting with negative decimals (e.g., `.93`, `.837`, `-1.58`) which suggests the path data is truncated or corrupted. This should be reviewed against the original Bootstrap Icons implementation to ensure the icon renders correctly.

comments.body: `logger.error` is currently called with `err.message`, which drops the stack trace and makes production debugging much harder. Consider logging the full error object (or `err.stack` alongside the message) while still persisting `err.message` to the DB if needed.

`loadThread` repeats the same `Array.isArray(res.data) ? res.data : []` normalization twice; consider assigning it once (e.g., `const threadData = ...`) and reusing for both `setThread` and the `hasUnread` check to reduce duplication and keep the logic consistent.

`data.phoneNumbers` is modeled as an array of strings, but `phoneRepository.syncPhones` expects items shaped like `{ phone_number, is_primary, label }` (see `server/repositories/phoneRepository.js:37-46`). Using realistic test data here helps ensure call sites match the repository contract and avoids normalizing the wrong API shape in tests.

`jest.clearAllMocks()` runs after setting `pool.getConnection.mockResolvedValue(mockConn)`. While `clearAllMocks` currently only clears call history, placing it first (then setting `mockResolvedValue`) avoids confusion and makes the setup order unambiguous.

The module under test (`insuranceService`) is required before the `jest.mock(...)` declarations. Without hoisting, `insuranceService` will load real `../db` and repository modules and then keep them cached, so the mocks won’t take effect (and tests may touch real MariaDB config). Move the `jest.mock` calls above the `require('./insuranceService')` (or require the service after mocks, e.g. inside `beforeEach` via `jest.isolateModules`).

`restoreService` is required before the `jest.mock(...)` calls. In CommonJS, this can cause the module under test to load the real `../db`, `../utils/audit`, and `bcrypt` modules before the mocks apply (potentially hitting a real DB connection and making the test nondeterministic). Move the `jest.mock(...)` declarations above the `require('./restoreService')`, or require `restoreService` only after mocks are set (e.g., inside `jest.isolateModules`).

The mock for `conn.query` returns an array for `INSERT INTO users` (e.g., `[{ insertId: 42 }]`), but the MariaDB driver used in this repo returns an object with `insertId` for inserts (see usage patterns like `const result = await conn.query(...); result.insertId`). This mismatch can let tests pass even if the real code would fail. Update the mock (and ideally `restoreService`’s destructuring of insert results) so the mocked return shape matches MariaDB’s actual `query` return value for INSERTs.

The test mocks for `conn.query()` return shapes (e.g., `[{ insertId: 10 }]` for INSERT and `[[{ id: 1 }]]` for SELECT) don’t match how this repo’s MariaDB driver is used elsewhere (SELECT returns an array of rows; INSERT returns a result object with `insertId`). As written, the tests may pass while masking a production bug in `restoreService`’s destructuring of query results. Consider updating the mocks to mirror real `mariadb` returns and adjusting `restoreService` accordingly so the test suite validates real runtime behavior.

`req` is initialized as `{ user: { id: 1 } }`, but the codebase (and `utils/audit.logAction`) consistently uses `req.user.user_id`. Using the real shape here will make the tests more representative and prevent future failures if `restoreService` starts reading `req.user.user_id` directly.

`restoreService` is required before the `jest.mock(...)` declarations. While Jest often hoists `jest.mock` calls, keeping mocks above the module import (or requiring the module after mocks are set up) avoids subtle ordering issues and makes the test behavior transformer-independent.

`jest.mock('../../services/insuranceService')` is declared after requiring `insuranceController`. This relies on Jest's hoisting behavior; if hoisting is disabled/changed (or when migrating to ESM), the controller may import the real service (and transitively load DB/pool code) before the mock is applied. Move the `jest.mock(...)` call above the `require('../../controllers/insuranceController')` to ensure the dependency is mocked before the controller module is evaluated.

In the error-path test, `createInsurance` should still be asserted to have been called with `req.body` (currently `{}`), not just “called”. Adding the argument assertion makes the test verify the controller’s delegation behavior consistently across both success and failure paths.

`jest.mock('../services/holidayService')` is declared after `require('./holidayController')` / `require('../services/holidayService')`. Without a Babel transform that hoists `jest.mock` calls, the controller will capture the real service module before it’s mocked, and `holidayService.addHoliday.mockResolvedValue(...)` will throw because `addHoliday` isn’t a Jest mock. Move the `jest.mock` call above all `require` statements (or require the controller after mocking) to ensure the mock is applied deterministically.

`insuranceService` is required before the `jest.mock(...)` calls. In CommonJS this can cause the service to load real repository modules before the mocks are applied, making the test either hit real DB code or fail when attempting to call `.mockResolvedValue` on non-mock functions. Move the `jest.mock` declarations above the `require('./insuranceService')` (or require the service inside the tests after mocking / use `jest.isolateModules`).

The mocked phone number objects use fields like `number`/`type`, but `phoneRepository.findByEntity` returns `phone_number`/`label`/`is_primary` (see `server/repositories/phoneRepository.js`). Using realistic field names here will make the test better reflect production behavior and reduce the chance of the test staying green while the real contract changes.

The `afterAll` block calls `require('../../db')` and then `pool.end()`, but since `../../db` is mocked in this test file, this will only ever call the mocked `end()` (and won’t close a real pool if one was created earlier due to module load order). If the goal is just to ensure Jest exits cleanly, consider removing this cleanup and instead ensure the real `db.js` is never imported (by ordering mocks first / using explicit repository mocks), or explicitly close the real pool via `jest.requireActual('../../db')` if you intentionally create it.

Test description says it "should create and return a holiday", but `HolidayService.addHoliday()` just returns whatever `holidayRepository.create()` returns (in production the repository returns the DB insert result, not a full holiday object). Consider renaming the test case to reflect the actual contract (e.g., "should pass data to repository and return its result") to avoid misleading future readers.

The mocks are declared after the initial `require` calls and also rely on Jest’s automatic module mocking for `holidayRepository`. This can be fragile because automocking may load the real repository to infer its shape, which in turn imports `db.js` and creates a real MariaDB pool at require-time. To make the tests deterministic (and avoid open-handle hangs), move mocks above all `require`s and/or provide an explicit mock factory for `holidayRepository` (e.g., `{ findAll: jest.fn(), create: jest.fn(), delete: jest.fn() }`) so the real module is never evaluated.

The timezone/date-mocking explanation comment is internally inconsistent (it says to use “midnight UTC” but the fixed date used is noon UTC) and includes conversational text (“Wait,”). This makes the intent harder to follow; please tighten/correct the comment to match the actual fixed timestamp and keep it concise.

`syncAppointmentPaymentStatus` lost the class-level indentation and now starts at column 0. While JS will still parse, it’s inconsistent with the rest of the class methods and may fail formatting/lint rules; re-indent it to match the surrounding method definitions.

This looks like a one-off codemod script that rewrites `financeService.js` via regex/string replacement. Committing it at repo root is risky (easy to run accidentally and silently rewrite source) and it’s not part of runtime behavior. Consider removing it from the PR, or moving it under `scripts/` with clear documentation and safeguards (e.g., explicit confirmation / dry-run).

Benchmark harness is being added at repo root and monkey-patches production modules (`pool.getConnection`, repositories). If this is only for local perf testing, consider moving it under `scripts/` (or a `benchmarks/` folder) and documenting that it’s not meant for production/deployments, to avoid accidental execution or confusion.

Bulk update uses `description = CONCAT(description, ' - Paid by Inst')`, but `transactions.description` is nullable. In MariaDB/MySQL, `CONCAT(NULL, ...)` returns `NULL`, so this will wipe the description for rows where it is currently NULL. Use `COALESCE(description, '')` (or similar) in the CONCAT, or set an explicit default string when description is NULL.

This assertion doesn’t actually verify that the *same* error object is rethrown—`toThrow(someOtherError)` mainly matches on message. If the intent is to ensure `addHoliday` rethrows the original error (including custom properties), assert identity (e.g., `rejects.toBe(someOtherError)`) or check relevant properties explicitly.

The test script uses `jest --forceExit`, which can mask open handles (e.g., DB pools, timers) and cause Jest to exit before cleanup completes. Prefer fixing the underlying open handle (typically by preventing DB modules from being imported in unit tests, or closing the pool in `afterAll`) and run Jest without `--forceExit` (optionally add `--detectOpenHandles` while debugging).

`package-lock.json` currently pins Jest to `^30.3.0`, but `package.json` sets it to `^29.7.0`. This mismatch will break `npm ci` / reproducible installs. Align the Jest version with the lockfile (or update the lockfile in the PR after changing the version).

`jest.mock('../../repositories/holidayRepository')` is declared after requiring `holidayService` / `holidayRepository`. This makes the test rely on Jest's mock-hoisting behavior; if hoisting/transform changes, the real repository (and `db` pool side effects) can be loaded before the mock. Move the `jest.mock(...)` call above the `require(...)` statements, or require the service inside `jest.isolateModules()` after mocking, to ensure the DB layer is never imported during unit tests.

These update methods return `null` when no allowed fields remain after filtering. Callers like `DoctorManagementController.updateDoctor` currently always return success, so a payload with only disallowed/typoed fields will be silently ignored. Consider throwing a validation error (or at least returning a consistent result object) so the API can respond with a 4xx and clients can detect mistakes.

The allowlist filtering logic is duplicated across `create`, `updateById`, `updateByUserId`, and `updateAfipSettings`. This makes it easier for the allowlist to drift or for fixes to be applied inconsistently. Consider extracting a small helper (and using a `Set` for membership checks) to centralize this logic.

`updateAfipSettings` uses the full `ALLOWED_FIELDS` list, so it can update many non-AFIP columns despite the method name implying a narrow scope. To avoid accidental misuse (especially if a controller ever forwards request bodies here), consider using a dedicated AFIP-only allowlist inside this method.

`ALLOWED_FIELDS` includes `user_id`, which means `updateByUserId`/`updateById` will allow changing the row ownership (`SET user_id = ?`). Since `updateByUserId` is called with user-supplied profile updates (e.g., `ProfileService.updateProfile`), this can enable privilege escalation / account reassignment. Consider using separate allowlists per operation (e.g., allow `user_id` only in `create`, and explicitly forbid it in all update methods).

`setSelectedDate` is destructured from `handlers` but never used in this component. With the project’s ESLint script (`client/package.json` has `eslint .`), this is likely to trigger `no-unused-vars`. Remove it from the destructuring list (or use it if intended).

This `lint_results_2.txt` file appears to be generated local lint output and is unlikely to be something we want to version. Please remove it from the repo (or move the information into the PR description) so it doesn’t become a maintained artifact.

This `lint_results_3.txt` file appears to be generated local lint output and is unlikely to be something we want to version. Please remove it from the repo (or move the information into the PR description) so it doesn’t become a maintained artifact.

In `useDoctors`, `loading` is never set to `true` when the request starts (it’s only set to `false` in the handlers), so consumers will never see a loading state during the initial fetch. Set `setLoading(true)` before calling `api.get('/users/doctors')` (and consider setting it in the `!hasFetched` branch).

This removed the `OPEN_USER_MODAL` window event listener, but other parts of the app still dispatch that event (e.g. `client/src/features/users/AdminUsersPage.jsx` and `components/UserManager.jsx`). As a result, those “Add user” buttons will no longer open the modal. Either restore the event listener here, or refactor the callers to open the modal via props/state instead of a global event.

The added `isMounted` guard here is redundant (there’s no async work in this effect) and it doesn’t address the `react-hooks/set-state-in-effect` lint errors still reported for `setCurrentMonth` / `setHasInitialized` in this effect (and for `setHasInitialized(false)` in the previous effect). If the goal is to eliminate setState-in-effect warnings, consider deriving the initial month outside effects (or setting it at the point where the modal is opened), or explicitly disable the rule for this effect with a justification if this pattern is intended.

These `lint_results*.txt` files look like generated local artifacts (captured console output) and don’t appear to be part of the app/runtime. Please remove them from the repository and rely on CI logs or attach them to the PR description instead, to avoid noise and merge conflicts.

`__dirname` is not available in Node ESM (which Vite uses for `vite.config.js`), so this alias resolution can throw at runtime and also triggers the current ESLint `no-undef` error. Compute the directory via `import.meta.url` (e.g., `fileURLToPath`/`path.dirname`) or switch the config to CJS so `__dirname` exists.

`process.env.NODE_ENV` is not defined in Vite client bundles unless you polyfill `process`, and ESLint already reports `process` as `no-undef`. Use `import.meta.env.DEV` / `import.meta.env.MODE` (or inject a `define` in Vite) for the development-only details block to avoid a runtime ReferenceError in production builds.

`useAppointmentsPageController` pulls permission flags from `usePermissions()` (`isStaff`, `isAdmin`, `isDoctor`, `isPatient`, `isMedicalStaff`), but they are not included in the returned controller object. `AppointmentsPage.jsx` destructures and uses these flags (e.g. to show staff-only tabs / doctor filter), so they will be `undefined` and those UI sections will never render. Return these permission flags from the controller (or stop destructuring them from `controller` and call `usePermissions()` in the page).

In a Vite app, `process` is typically not defined in the browser. `process.env.NODE_ENV` here can cause a runtime `ReferenceError: process is not defined`, preventing the error UI from rendering. Prefer `import.meta.env.DEV` / `import.meta.env.MODE` for the dev-only details check.

This component no longer listens for the `OPEN_USER_MODAL` window event, but other code still dispatches it (e.g. `AdminUsersPage` / `UserManager`). As a result, clicking those "Agregar Usuario" buttons will do nothing. Either restore the event listener here or update the dispatching components to call `openModal('CREATE')` through props/context instead of a global event.

This new service is implemented as a class instance, but the other services in `client/src/services` export plain objects with async functions. Consider aligning with the existing pattern to reduce boilerplate and keep the services layer consistent (also makes mocking simpler in tests).

There’s a lot of duplicated `lazy(() => import(...).then(m => ({ default: m.X })))` boilerplate here. Consider extracting a small helper (e.g. `lazyNamed(modulePath, exportName)`) to make this list easier to maintain and reduce the risk of copy/paste mistakes when adding/removing routes.

`client/package.json` sets `"type": "module"`, so this Vite config is executed as ESM and `__dirname` is not defined. As written, `path.resolve(__dirname, './src')` will throw at startup. Use an ESM-safe approach (e.g., derive the directory from `import.meta.url`, or use `new URL('./src', import.meta.url)` with `fileURLToPath`).

The lazy-loaded page declarations are very repetitive and hard to scan/maintain (each route repeats the same `import(...).then(...)` unwrapping pattern). Consider extracting a small helper (e.g., `lazyNamed(path, exportName)`) or grouping per-feature imports to reduce duplication and make future route additions less error-prone.

The repository module exports a class instance (`module.exports = new HolidayRepository()`), so Jest's automatic mocking may not generate `create`/etc. as `jest.fn()`s because the methods live on the prototype (not as own properties). This makes `holidayRepository.create.mockResolvedValue(...)` unreliable (likely `create` is undefined). Prefer providing an explicit mock factory for `../repositories/holidayRepository` that defines `create: jest.fn()` (and any other methods used), or switch to `jest.spyOn` on the real module export.

`package-lock.json` is present in the repo, but this PR adds a new devDependency (`jest`) without updating the lockfile. Please regenerate/commit the updated lockfile so installs are deterministic and CI uses the same dependency graph.

`jest.mock('../repositories/holidayRepository')` is declared after requiring `./holidayService`. Since `holidayService` imports the repository at module load time, this can result in the real repository being captured before the mock is applied (and the tests will fail unless a transform hoists the mock). Move the `jest.mock(...)` call above the `require('./holidayService')` (or require the service after mocking) so the dependency is reliably mocked.
